subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo - next steps and model shortlist

Hi Sara -

Thanks again for taking the time to demo Acme's use case this morning. Great conversation - especially around the multi-turn context window for customer support and the need to keep average token latency under 120ms for edge interactions. Per our chat, I pulled together a concise shortlist of models to evaluate (attached) and a recommended evaluation prompt set to validate hallucination/consistency on your corpus.

High-level notes and asks: 
- Primary objectives: high answer accuracy for policy/knowledge responses, consistent latency <=120ms (p95 for a 512-token response), and predictable per-token cost under $0.0006.
- Constraints: data residency in us-east, SOC2 controls, and evaluating on a sample of 10k anonymized convo turns you already shared.

What I attached: acme-model-shortlist.xlsx (three candidates + rationale), acme-benchmark-summary.pdf (initial perf numbers from our pre-demo sweep), acme-eval-promptset.jsonl (prompt set + expected behaviors).

Recommended next steps: 
1) Your team to run the eval prompt set against the shortlisted checkpoints (we can host a free eval run on Redwood Dedicated for 72 hours).
2) Rishi to share exact inference configs and cost estimate (batching, KV cache settings, quantization profile).
3) If results look good, schedule a 60-min technical sync to agree on rollout plan and SLA.

I'll summarize the shortlist and rationale below in case it's useful for your procurement review.

- - Shortlist (summary) - -
- redwood-3.1-base (intended as a high-quality, lower-latency baseline): best cost/latency balance for deterministic Q&A workloads. Expected p95 latency ~90-110ms on Dedicated T4-equivalent with 512 tokens, good factuality on policy retrieval prompts.
- open-llama-70b-q4 (quantized): higher raw quality on nuanced instructions; higher cost and memory footprint - recommended for fallback/complex responses where correctness > cost. p95 latency ~140-170ms in our test; can be reduced with nvidia A100 or increased batching but at cost of higher queueing.
- instr-lite-13b-quant (13B quantized optimized): sweet spot for low-cost deployments with decent instruction-following and very low SLOs; p95 latency ~50-80ms and cost per token significantly lower. Risk: occasional hallucination on policy edge cases; needs prompt anchoring and retrieval integration.

I'll follow up with Rishi on the exact config for the dedicated eval job.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Santini <paul.santini@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo - next steps and model shortlist

Marissa -

Thanks for the quick summary and attachments. This is very helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side before we run evals internally: 

1) For "redwood-3.1-base" - is that a Redwood-maintained variant of an open checkpoint? Any guarantees / known regression windows?
2) For the quantized 70B, can you share memory footprint and recommended instance types so we can check with infra?
3) For instr-lite-13b-quant, can you call out the prompt anchoring patterns you recommend (we saw a few hallucinations in the demo).

Also, procurement asked for a ballpark monthly cost estimate for a Dedicated dev environment (enough throughput to run 10k evals/day and an integration test harness). If you can provide an initial number, that will help speed contracting.

We can start the eval run next Tuesday if Redwood can stand up the test environment and share results + raw logits (or evaluation traces) for our analysis.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Platform, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo - next steps and model shortlist

Sara - thanks for the questions. Answers inline and additional detail below.

1) redwood-3.1-base - short answer: Redwood-curated variant derived from an open LLM with production profiling and ongoing quality monitoring. We maintain a rolling performance/regression dashboard and will notify customers of major model changes; for Dedicated customers you can pin exact model hashes to avoid drift. No "guarantee" of upstream changes, but we provide pinned model versioning and change logs.

2) open-llama-70b-q4 - memory & instance guidance: a single A100-80GB or 2xH100-80GB (for high concurrency) is recommended for low-latency serving; quantized q4 reduced footprint to ~40-45GB but peak KV cache still impacts memory. For our Dedicated dev eval (non-production) we can run on a single A100; expected p95 latency in our internal sweep was 150ms for 512-token responses. We'll include config YAML in the eval package.

3) instr-lite-13b-quant prompt anchoring: 
- Always include a short system prompt that defines role and response constraints (e.g., "Answer using only the policy content. If unsure, say 'I don't know.'").
- Use retrieval-augmented answers: add a retrieved_context block of 3-5 highest-similarity snippets (we recommend stored embeddings with a 1536-d vector).
- Use few-shot positive/negative examples for policy edge cases in the prompt.

Procurement cost ballpark (very rough): 
- Dedicated dev environment to run 10k evals/day (mixed lengths, average 250 tokens request + 400 tokens response): ~$3,500- $5,000/month on Dedicated T4/A100 mix depending on reserved commit and caching savings.
- Hosted API equivalent (on-demand) is ~25-40% higher for the same throughput.

What we'll provide for the eval run next Tuesday: 
- A pre-provisioned Dedicated eval instance for 72 hours (US-east), configured with the three model candidates and the eval prompt set.
- Raw evaluation traces (per-request latencies, logits, and top-k tokens) + our scoring script.
- A short post-eval writeup summarizing quality vs. latency vs. cost tradeoffs.

Action items: 
- I will ask Rishi to attach the exact YAML config and instance recommendation before EOD.
- Please confirm who on your side will own the eval run and share any additional acceptance criteria we should score against (e.g., F1 on retrieval QA, hallucination rate threshold).

CC'ing Stephanie (CS) for the eval orchestration and Rishi for config + perf.

Best,
Marissa

From: Paul Santini <paul.santini@acme.com>

This looks good to me. I'll own the eval run on Acme's side and can share the acceptance criteria: 
- F1 >= 0.92 on known retrieval QA set
- Hallucination rate <= 1.5% on the blind set
- p95 latency <= 120ms for 512-token responses (measured at our test harness)

Marissa / Rishi - please send the YAML config and the Dedicated dev instance details (IP, credentials, expiry for the 72h eval) and I'll schedule the run for Tue 10 Mar 2026 09:00 AM ET.
